images.caption: Figure 2:Overview of HEELO.Top:the agent-native primitive library, one box per family with the resource its primitives own.Middle:a real-world task enters as a task request with its context, constraints, and acceptance criteria; library selection and composition finds candidates through their interfaces, lets each assess its own relevance, and composes a task-specific graph whose activated primitives exchange messages, and three illustrative compositions are drawn on the right.Bottom:evidence-based execution runs and verifies the plan in the task’s environment, improvement traces a failure to the implicated primitives and revises only that work within a round budget, and validation and publishing adds a validated primitive to the library on a separate path. The bottom strip shows what an agent-native primitive holds: a resource, a resident LLM that serves as its natural-language interface, an interface through which a harness finds and invokes it, and an output of results and messages to other primitives.

header: 6.  The heelo.dev Platform for Real-World Tasks

images.caption: Figure 3:The heelo.dev platform.Agents such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor reach real-world tools through HEELO, which orchestrates agent-native primitives for each task: it plans the task, routes each need to a primitive, executes the primitives, and verifies the result, revising the plan when a check fails. Four loops test the platform end to end: distribution creates and publishes content across channels, acquisition finds potential customers and sends personalized outreach, the personal assistant takes over everyday tasks across apps and tools, and validation discovers real problems and validates market demand.

Figure 10:Overview of Agent Primitives.(a) Agent Primitives enable system-level functionality to be constructed by composing reusable latent operators, which replace manually designed agent roles and natural-language interaction protocols. (b)–(d) Three representative primitives: Review, Voting and Selection, and Planning and Execution, each encapsulating a recurring multi-agent computation pattern as a reusable latent operator. (e) A Knowledge Pool stores previously observed queries and effective system structures, providing structural guidance for system construction. (f) Internal coordination within and across primitives is carried out via latent KV cache communication[48].

Figure 11:Overview of HERMES.Dynamic activation selects the repository components relevant to the task and instantiates Dev-Primitives, which modify their own artifacts and exchange requirements in natural language. The modified repository is executed, and bug diagnosis maps the observed failure back to the components that must be revised, reactivating only those for the next round[49].

Figure 12:Overview of ANTMAN.(1) Static substrate map:a deterministic partition splits the information substrate, such as code, repositories, and documents, into fixed territories, each summarized by a WorkerCard, and every worker uses one shared toolbox.(2) Revisable Need Graph:the user query becomes unresolved information needs whose status, evidence, attempts, and progress are updated from each worker report; an LLM graph revision then adds, deletes, or updates needs, so that a need can be resolved or reframed and a new need can emerge.(3) Need-conditioned coordination:one open need is selected and routed through WorkerCard retrieval to one territory worker, which searches only its territory and returns evidence, progress, and uncertainty; the assessment closes, refines, or keeps the need open, repeated lack of progress triggers reframing, rerouting, or fallback, and the answer is synthesized from resolved evidence once the required needs are resolved or the budget is spent. The example follows the query “Which client.send callers need a timeout update?” over a small repository[50].

Figure 14:Overview of STITCH, shown with State Guard.(1) On development tasks kept apart from evaluation, recurring failures, such as an actor editing the original files whose details it later needs, are grouped into deficiencies; a candidate primitive is implemented and enters the frozen library only after it passes behavior tests and improves task success over the same harness without it, and each primitive carries an application scope and a composition contract. (2) Before the first actor request, the harness composer reads the task requirements, step budget, default workflow, and primitive interfaces and states a composition intent, which the deterministic compiler wires into a workflow; the graph is validated for supported primitives, compatible specifications, valid wiring, reachable termination, and bounded loops, an invalid graph is revised within a retry limit, and the default harness is used otherwise. (3) The compiled harness then runs fixed: its hooks save copies before each action, check the originals after it, and restore and report any change to the actor[51].
